articles.title: Draymond Green sends a message about the Warriors' rookie who has stepped up in the absence of the injured Curry: “Lower your expectations”
articles.standfirst: Draymond Green calls for patience as Yaxel Lendeborg faces growing responsibilities
articles.summary: Draymond Green calls for patience as Yaxel Lendeborg faces growing responsibilities
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors’ struggles without Stephen Curry have placed an unexpected spotlight on rookie Yaxel Lendeborg . With their offensive leader sidelined, Golden State has increasingly relied on the 24-year-old to create scoring opportunities and help organize the offense.

However, Draymond Green believes the team needs to reconsider how much responsibility it's placing on the young player.

Green shared his thoughts following the Warriors’ 115-94 defeat to the New Orleans Pelicans, their third consecutive loss.

“Depend on him, but lower the expectations,’ Green said.

“Sounds unfair to him to try to make him step into Steph’s role, 13 games into the schedule. So depend on him like we need to, but lower what we’re expecting to allow him to ease his flow into it. I think right now we’re putting too much pressure on him. It’s tough to deal with.”

Lendeborg's performance against New Orleans showed why Golden State continues to trust him. The rookie finished with 28 points and eight rebounds, which highlighted his ability to contribute offensively despite the team's disappointing result. However, his individual production couldn't prevent another defeat, as the Warriors struggled throughout the contest.

Golden State was outscored 35-11 in the opening quarter and converted just 11 of its 46 three-point attempts. The Pelicans also controlled the boards, winning the rebounding battle 58-50.

Steve Kerr wants the rookie to learn from difficult experiences

The latest defeat followed an equally frustrating performance against the San Antonio Spurs. In that 123-85 blowout, Lendeborg managed only three points on 1-of-13 shooting and finished with a minus-40 rating.

The rookie later admitted that the disappointing performance had affected him mentally. He subsequently arrived at practice with a new haircut, describing the change as a fresh beginning.

Head coach Steve Kerr understands the challenges facing his young player. He believes experiencing difficult moments is an unavoidable part of developing in the NBA.

"He's a rookie. This is his first year, and we're putting an enormous responsibility on his shoulders, and so he has to go through this," Kerr said.

"There's no way around it. You can't cheat your way through that. You have to feel the highs and the lows."

Meanwhile, Curry's absence remains Golden State's biggest concern. The superstar is dealing with a right oblique abdominal tear and is expected to be re-evaluated on November 26. The Warriors haven't established a definitive timetable for his return.

Golden State has now dropped to 8-6 after beginning the season 8-3.

articles.title: LeBron James blames Michael Jordan for his “bad habits”: “You don’t realize it... he’s been doing it for years and years.”
articles.standfirst: The NBA superstar reveals how imitating his childhood idol led to shooting habits he still recognizes today
articles.summary: The NBA superstar reveals how imitating his childhood idol led to shooting habits he still recognizes today
articles.body:
LeBron James has spent much of his basketball career being compared with Michael Jordan, but the four-time NBA MVP has now admitted that trying to imitate the Chicago Bulls legend also left him developing some bad habits that took time to recognize and correct.

Speaking on the Mind the Game podcast alongside former NBA star Steve Nash, James discussed how watching Jordan influenced his shooting technique during his younger years.

The Lakers legend explained that he was fascinated by Jordan's signature fadeaway jumper and wanted to recreate the move without fully understanding the mechanics that made it so effective.

“My shooting journey is literally like watching Michael Jordan. I didn’t realize how balanced Michael Jordan was (shooting) a fadeaway. I saw the fadeaway,” James said.

“When I started seeing that I had some athletic genes, I may have picked up some bad habits in my shooting because I can emulate that.

“So, I was shooting fadeaways as a freshman in high school, and I would make them, but I didn’t realize I was picking up bad habits… but I didn’t realize that I was picking up bad habits along that time because I didn’t study the fact that, okay, yeah, MJ is doing that, but you’re not even seeing how on balance he is. He’s been doing that for years and years.”

He also admitted that his fascination with Jordan's game sometimes prevented him from taking full advantage of his own athletic abilities, particularly when attacking the basket.

LeBron James learned an important lesson from imitating Michael Jordan

While Jordan's influence on an entire generation of players is undeniable, James eventually understood that replicating a signature move doesn't necessarily mean replicating the skills required to execute it successfully.

Interestingly, the conversation comes as James navigates another adjustment in Philadelphia. The 76ers have enjoyed an impressive beginning to the 2026-27 season, opening with a 12-3 record to establish themselves at the top of the Eastern Conference.

However, James hasn't enjoyed his usual scoring production. The 41-year-old is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists per game, while his three-point shooting percentage has dropped to 22.5 per cent.

A report also suggested that James had asked Philadelphia's coaching staff for patience as he worked towards regaining his conditioning and shooting rhythm, potentially by December. However, the veteran forward quickly rejected the suggestion on social media, making it clear that he hadn't made the reported request.

Despite his scoring struggles, James continues to contribute in other areas. He recently climbed into third place on the NBA's all-time assists leaderboard, while Philadelphia continues winning as its new-look lineup builds chemistry around Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid.

articles.title: LeBron James gets added to the Sixers’ group chat: “LeBron was added to the group”
articles.standfirst: The veteran is finding a new sense of team chemistry in Philadelphia
articles.summary: The veteran is finding a new sense of team chemistry in Philadelphia
articles.body:
L eBron James may have taken a subtle shot at the Los Angeles Lakers following a recent interview, as his experience with the Philadelphia 76ers appears to be giving him a different perspective on team chemistry. Despite the age difference between James and some of his new teammates, the veteran seems to be enjoying the environment in Philadelphia and the way the group has welcomed him.

James revealed that he had been added to the Sixers' group chat, something he said was not part of the team culture during his earlier years in the NBA. The comment raised some eyebrows, particularly because modern communication was already common during his time with the Lakers. His remarks seemed to suggest that the relationships players build outside the locker room were not necessarily as strong during his previous experience in Los Angeles.

Building chemistry beyond basketball

Things have been different in Philadelphia, where players have made an effort to spend time together away from the court. Team dinners, casual get-togethers and even attending a comedy show have become part of the group's routine, helping them develop a connection that goes beyond practices and games.

That environment has also given James a sense of support from his teammates . With the veteran spending less time around his family during this new chapter, having teammates who invite him to join them and make sure he is included has become another important part of his transition to Philadelphia.

A mutual benefit in Philadelphia

There were questions about the 76ers' decision to bring James into the team, but the early signs suggest the move is working for both sides. Philadelphia gets an experienced leader who understands what it takes to compete at the highest level, while James has joined a group that could help him continue adding to his legacy.

The connection between James and his teammates could also play an important role as the season progresses . His influence extends beyond the locker room, with younger players able to learn from his experience and look to him as someone who can guide the group through the challenges of an NBA season.

The Sixers are focused on producing results and competing for an NBA championship, while also giving James another opportunity to add to his already impressive basketball history . With the group continuing to build its chemistry through shared experiences, the team chat has become another place where those relationships can grow, and perhaps where some basketball conversations take place as well.

articles.title: Lakers’ hot start raises a big question: Was LeBron James leaving the best thing?
articles.standfirst: The early results of the team lead by Luka Doncic are difficult to ignore
articles.summary: The early results of the team lead by Luka Doncic are difficult to ignore
articles.body:
T he Los Angeles Lakers are looking more like championship contenders with every passing game, and their remarkable start to the 2026-27 NBA season is bringing back memories of some of the franchise’s greatest teams.

At 12-2, the Purple and Gold are off to one of their best starts since the turn of the century. They have matched the San Antonio Spurs’ record and won eight consecutive games, while their offensive production has made them one of the most difficult teams in the league to contain.

But there is another storyline behind Los Angeles’ resurgence: the possibility that LeBron James’ departure was exactly what the franchise needed to move forward. James was the face of the Lakers for years, leading the organization to the 2020 NBA championship and delivering another era of memorable moments.

However, the current team appears to have found a different identity, one built around Luka Doncic's playmaking , defensive disruption and a faster style of basketball. And the early results are difficult to ignore.

A start worthy of the Lakers’ championship history

Los Angeles has won at least 12 of its first 14 games only five times since 2000. The previous four occasions offer an encouraging historical comparison. The Lakers opened the 2001-02 season 13-1 and went on to win the NBA championship. They repeated that 13-1 start in 2008-09, again finishing the season with the Larry O’Brien Trophy.

The 2010-11 team also started 12-2 but was eliminated in the Western Conference semifinals . Most recently, the 2019-20 Lakers opened with the same 12-2 record before winning the championship in the NBA’s Orlando bubble.

That means three of the previous four teams to reach this mark eventually captured the title. It is obviously too early to put this year’s squad in that category, but the comparison highlights just how impressive the start has been.

Luka has been central to the turnaround. The Lakers are averaging an NBA-best 122.8 points per game, and their offensive rating is also the best in the league. Yet the most interesting part of their success is how they are generating those opportunities. Yet the most interesting part of their success is how they are generating those opportunities.

Luka Dončić and a new Lakers identity

The Lakers have embraced a philosophy that takes full advantage of Doncic's extraordinary ability to create offense. With a generational playmaker running the show, generating more possessions gives Los Angeles more opportunities to exploit defensive mismatches and create scoring chances.

The team has moved from 22nd in total possessions last season to seventh entering Monday. But that does not mean the Lakers are rushing their offense. They rank among the league’s top eight in both late and very late shot-clock frequency, showing a willingness to let Luka control the tempo and find the right opportunity.

The other side of the equation is defense. Los Angeles ranks just 17th defensively, but its ability to disrupt opponents has become a defining characteristic. The Lakers lead the NBA with 11 steals per game and rank third in both forced turnovers, at 18.4, and blocks, at 6.4.

That pressure is not coming from one superstar. Seven different Lakers are averaging at least one steal per game, a level of collective defensive activity unmatched by any other team with at least 10 games played. The offense then turns those mistakes into points. Los Angeles leads the NBA with 24.4 points per game off turnovers.

The Lakers have become only the second team since 1980 to average at least 120 points while recording 150 or more steals and 80 or more blocks through the first 14 games of a season.

Was LeBron James’ departure a blessing in disguise?

It would be premature to suggest that the Lakers are better simply because James is no longer in Los Angeles . His contributions to the franchise, including the 2020 championship, are undeniable. But the current team’s early success does raise an interesting question about the direction of the organization.

For years, the Lakers’ identity was closely tied to James and his ability to control games. Now, Doncic has become the centerpiece of an offense that emphasizes pace, ball movement and creating additional possessions. The supporting cast has also embraced a collective defensive approach that gives Los Angeles another way to win when its shots are not falling.

That change could prove significant over the course of a long season. Instead of relying on one superstar to carry the team, the Lakers are developing an identity that involves contributions from across the roster.

Of course, the real test will come against the Western Conference’s best teams and in the playoffs, where defensive weaknesses and roster depth become much more difficult to hide.

For now, however, Los Angeles has every reason to feel encouraged. Its 12-2 record puts it in rare company, its eight-game winning streak has generated momentum, and its statistical profile evokes memories of the Showtime era.

articles.title: Golden State Warriors exploring big trade to give Stephen Curry one last title run
articles.standfirst: Golden State isn’t ready to give up on another title run. With Curry still playing at an elite level, the Warriors could be preparing a blockbuster trade before the deadline.
articles.summary: Golden State isn’t ready to give up on another title run. With Curry still playing at an elite level, the Warriors could be preparing a blockbuster trade before the deadline.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors made it clear they still have life in the championship race. Before Stephen Curry suffered an oblique injury, the franchise was enjoying its best stretch of the season with an eight-game winning streak, proving the roster still has enough talent to compete with the NBA ’s elite.

Although the absence of their superstar has led to some stumbles, the front office remains confident in the group’s potential and appears willing to make a decisive move. According to new league-wide rumors, Golden State is scanning the trade market for a new piece who can complement Curry in the final stretch of his historic career.

The two-time MVP will still miss several more weeks , but the Warriors have attractive assets — including Jimmy Butler , Draymond Green , Kristaps Porzingis , and Brandin Podziemski — that could help them land a high-impact addition before the trade deadline.

The franchise’s objective is clear: find one last elite running mate for Curry and make another serious push for a title that would further cement one of the most important dynasties in recent NBA history .

Warriors prepare for a possible market splash

On ESPN’s NBA Today , analysts Marc Spears , Tim McMahon , and former NBA champion Kendrick Perkins discussed the possibility of Golden State executing a major deal to add another star and capitalize on its strong start to the 2026-27 season .

“It’s not just about who’s in free agency, it’s about what you can do in the trade market,” McMahon said regarding the Warriors’ ability to add talent in the near future, while ruling out Anthony Davis as a realistic trade target.

Spears was more direct, stating that he expects an aggressive approach from the organization before the deadline.

“I expect the Warriors, and I think they need to be aggressive at the trade deadline,” Spears added. “They have some pieces to do it. There might be some people that have been there a while that could be traded (like) Draymond, Jimmy… I do expect the Warriors to make a splash at the trade deadline.”

While Kristaps Porzingis has been mentioned in connection with Golden State, there has also been speculation that Jimmy Butler or Draymond Green could be used as centerpieces in a large-scale deal if the franchise decides to go all-in for another title in the Curry era.

Curry himself has acknowledged that he is likely in the final contractual phase of his career, giving the Warriors a limited window to surround him with the necessary talent and chase one more championship.

The front office has not yet settled on a primary target, but the message appears clear: Golden State wants to maximize Curry’s current level and is not willing to wait much longer to compete for a title again.

The franchise fell short in previous attempts to land Giannis Antetokounmpo and could not convince LeBron James to join the Bay. Yet as long as Curry continues to perform at an All-NBA level, the Warriors will remain an attractive destination for any star looking to contend for a championship.

articles.title: Inside Kevin Durant’s $13.9 million mansion now back on the market
articles.standfirst: The Houston Rockets star’s Arizona property has returned to the market with a multimillion-dollar asking price and several standout features.
articles.summary: The Houston Rockets star’s Arizona property has returned to the market with a multimillion-dollar asking price and several standout features.
articles.body:
Kevin Durant is used to making headlines for what he does on the NBA court, but this time, one of his properties is drawing attention. The basketball star has relisted his mansion in Paradise Valley, Arizona, for $13.9 million. He purchased the home in September 2023 for $12.95 million, shortly after joining the Phoenix Suns from the Brooklyn Nets .

The property first hit the market in September 2025 with an asking price of $14.5 million. By March 2026, the price had dropped to just under $14 million, before the listing was taken down in September. Now, the mansion is back on the market with a new asking price below its original listing .

But what makes this property worth $13.9 million?

Located between Phoenix and Scottsdale, the mansion offers 10,865 square feet of living space on a 1.72-acre lot . Its distinctive U-shaped architecture gives the home a unique look, while mountain views and the privacy of its surroundings add to its appeal.

Inside, the residence features four bedrooms and seven bathrooms. Outside, a heated swimming pool and spa offer plenty of ways to enjoy Arizona's warm weather, while the garage has room for up to eight vehicles.

Paradise Valley is one of Arizona's most exclusive communities. Its luxury homes have long attracted professional athletes and business executives, making the area a highly sought-after destination for buyers looking for this level of privacy and comfort.

Meanwhile, Durant continues his career with the Houston Rockets, where he is playing his 20th NBA season . The mansion remains a reminder of his time with the Phoenix Suns, but it is now ready for a new owner. The question is whether this latest listing will finally bring the buyer the property has been waiting for.

articles.title: Drake gifts Raptors fan Mackenzie and her son $100,000 as Knicks beat Toronto on the road
articles.standfirst: The holiday-season surprise also came with two courtside seats for the Raptors’ next game, against the Washington Wizards
articles.summary: The holiday-season surprise also came with two courtside seats for the Raptors’ next game, against the Washington Wizards
articles.body:
As the Knicks beat the Raptors 111–102 in Toronto, Drake turned a timeout into a $100,000 surprise for local fan Mackenzie and her son, Ezequiel. The broadcast announcer confirmed the amount as the two stood with Drake courtside during OVO Night.

According to blogTO, Drake said he was feeling festive for the holiday season and wanted to surprise two local fans. The gift was a check, and he also gave Mackenzie and Ezequiel two courtside tickets to the Raptors’ next game, against the Washington Wizards on Nov. 18. Scotiabank Arena.

Drake’s gift came during OVO Night’s return

The Raptors’ annual OVO Night returned after two seasons away. The event celebrates the team’s partnership with Drake’s Toronto-based brand, October’s Very Own, and featured special programming and an exclusive merchandise collection at Scotiabank Arena. Toronto Raptors

The surprise happened with 4:44 left in the third quarter, when the scoreboard showed New York leading 71–70. Toronto went into the fourth quarter ahead 83–80, but the Knicks outscored the Raptors 31–19 in the final period to pull away.

Jalen Brunson led all scorers with 31 points. Ja’Kobe Walter led Toronto with 25, followed by RJ Barrett with 22 and Scottie Barnes with 20. Karl-Anthony Towns recorded a double-double with 16 points and 16 rebounds.

articles.summary: Harper left late in San Antonio’s loss
articles.body:
D ylan Harper went down hard late in the San Antonio Spurs’ loss to the Detroit Pistons and needed help walking off the court. The rookie guard slipped while trying to catch a pass with 53.6 seconds remaining and did not return.

The fall appeared to leave Harper in pain . He stayed on the floor before getting back to his feet, and teammate Keldon Johnson helped him toward the locker room.

Harper’s status remains unclear

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said Harper appeared to slip and that he hoped the guard was OK, but he had no further information.

The awkward landing raised concern about a possible groin injury, though the team had not confirmed a diagnosis.

Harper finished with 20 points on 8-of-14 shooting, four rebounds and two assists.

Victor Wembanyama added 25 points and 18 rebounds , but Detroit won 105–93 behind 27 points from Cade Cunningham and 25 from Daniss Jenkins. The loss snapped San Antonio’s 12-game winning streak.
